 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Saints.
 Phillips hasn’t played since Week 6 because of the hamstring issue. One of Carolina’s biggest offseason additions, Phillips was off to a solid start to the year before going down. He had 2.5 sacks in five games, two of which he left early. Getting Phillips back will be a big win for the Panthers’ defense. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak 
 Source:  Ian Rapoport

 Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable for Week 10 against the Saints. 
 Despite the questionable designation, it’s safe to say Phillips is trending in the right direction after being upgraded to a full participant for Friday’s practice. Barring any unexpected setbacks, we would assume Phillips will be good to go against the Saints. The Saints also listed CB Will Lee (hamstring) and OL Brady Christensen (hamstring) as questionable, and CB Mike Jackson (groin) as doubtful.

 Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited on Thursday. 
 Phillips practiced in full yesterday. Today, he was only limited. Hm. Today’s lightened workload could be a planned load management decision, but tomorrow’s practice participation will be worth watching for the Panthers’ top pass rusher. The Panthers’ stud LG Damien Lewis (knee) was also downgraded today, while starting perimeter CB Mike Jackson (groin) remained a full participant.

 Panthers declared LB Jaelan Phillips, QB Haynes King, CB Will Lee III, RB AJ Dillon, LB Bobby Okereke, OG Damien Lewis, and DT TeRah Edwards inactive for Week 9 against the Broncos. 
 Phillips and Lewis were both ruled out before the weekend, so there’s nothing too surprising to see here. The Panthers hope to end a two-game losing streak this week at home against a stout Broncos defense.

 Panthers ruled out Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) for Week 9 against the Broncos. 
 Phillips did not practice at all this week, after sitting out the Panthers’ last two games. Losing a key edge rusher will make things harder for the Panthers’ defense. Bo Nix should have decently comfortable pockets, though.

 Carolina also ruled out left guard Damien Lewis, who is dealing with a knee issue. Phillips also missed last week’s game because of a hamstring injury. The hope is that the mini-bye after Thursday Night Football is enough to get him back for Week 9. Phillips has 2.5 sacks this year.

 Phillips is a big loss, but it’s an otherwise quiet list for the Panthers vs. a more-injured and undermanned Bucs squad. Phillips is week to week after pulling his hammy in Week 6 against the Eagles.

 Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) is questionable to return to Week 6 against the Eagles. 
 Phillips came into this game questionable with a hamstring injury but was able to suit up. Unfortunately, he got hurt early in the first quarter and is unlikely to return. Considering he had the bye week to heal and is not 100 percent, it seems likely that the EDGE rusher will miss some time with the injury.

 Taylor Moton (blood clots) is practicing in full for Week 6 against the Eagles. 
 Moton is tentatively on track to make his return from injured reserve this week. Meanwhile, RT Monroe Freeling (knee) sat out on Wednesday. Panthers DT Tershawn Wharton (neck) is practicing in full, while EDGE Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) was limited.

 Panthers head coach Dave Canales said he is “hopeful” Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) will be able to play in Week 6 against the Eagles. 
 Phillips went down with a hamstring injury late in Sunday’s game against the Lions and didn’t return to the field. For a player with Phillips’ injury history, there were immediate concerns regarding the severity of the injury, but with a Week 5 bye on tap, the hope is Phillips won’t miss much time, if any. Phillips has totaled two sacks in his first four games of the season. In addition to Phillips, the team is also hopeful that OT Monroe Freeling (knee) will be able to return in Week 6.

 #55 
 Devin Lloyd (calf) did not practice Wednesday. 
 Lloyd was one of the Panthers’ premier free agent additions this offseason, and he’s already proven to be worth the investment. Lloyd terrorized the Falcons in Week 2 with a sack and two interceptions, one of which was a pick-six. Fellow free agent acquisition Jaelan Phillips was also absent from practice today. He is dealing with a back injury. Though the Browns aren’t a particularly good offense right now, it would still be a massive boon for them if Lloyd and Phillips are out for Week 3.

 A.J. Brown (ankle/knee) is active for Week 10 against the Lions.
 Rhamondre Stevenson is also active. Brown made the trip to Germany and was limited in all three practices this week. He has been dealing with knee issues for several years, and we’re sure this isn’t the last we will hear of it in 2026. Still, he has been cleared for action today, meaning fantasy managers should get him in their lineups. We’re treating him as a volatile WR2. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Raiders planned to start Fernando Mendoza “in the next few weeks” even if Kirk Cousins had not been traded. 
 With games against the Seahawks and Broncos on tap for Mendoza’s first two starts, the Raiders may have wanted to throw Cousins to the wolves for those games before getting the No. 1 overall pick under center against Cleveland. Instead, the Vikings offered Vegas a third-round pick for Cousins and the Raiders couldn’t say no. Mendoza will make his first NFL start at home versus Seattle today. We expect him to be in the QB2 mix at some point this year, but it might take a few weeks given Vegas’s tough schedule. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak 
 Source:  Ian Rapoport

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports the Vikings have talked to Kirk Cousins “about returning to Minnesota for the 2027 season.”
 Rapoport notes that the Vikings told Cousins they wanted him around beyond this year before their trade for him was complete. They would go on to pay a third-round pick to reunite with their former starter. Even if Cousins is far from a superstar quarterback, head coach Kevin O’Connell is clearly sick of the weekly carousel under center. The Vikings will be legitimate Super Bowl contenders if Cousins can just play as well as he did in Vegas. A deep playoff run will all but guarantee him a spot on the roster next year. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Joey Porter Jr. (ankle) is “trending towards playing” in Week 10 against the 49ers. 
 Fellow Dallas cornerback Daron Bland is also expected to play. We don’t foresee the Cowboys putting up much of a fight against the 49ers offense, but having both corners available will at least help them slow San Francisco down a bit. Porter has appeared in four games for the Cowboys this year. He has three pass breakups and eight combined tackles.

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Jordan Addison (thumb) “will have his status determined closer to game time.”
 Addison injured his thumb in practice on Friday and the team listed him as questionable for today’s game. The team elevated wide receiver Jeshaun Jones from the practice squad yesterday, casting some doubt on Addison’s availability. With Jauan Jennings also out, Tai Felton and Myles Price could be in line for larger roles today.

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Will Anderson (ankle) is expected to play in Week 10 against the Browns. 
 Anderson was added to the injury report on Thursday, then downgraded to a DNP on Friday. He was on the report earlier this year with the ankle injury. We suspect it flared up on him mid-week. The good news for Texans fans is that it won’t stop him from facing the Browns. With 9.5 sacks to his name through eight games, Anderson is in the midst of another elite season. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports Garrett Wilson cleared the NFL’s concussion protocol and will play in Week 10 against the Bills.
 Wilson missed Week 9 because of the concussion but has cleared the league’s concussion protocol ahead of today’s game. Jets coach Aaron Glenn told reporters on Friday he expected Wilson to play, so this doesn’t come as much of a surprise. In a potential shootout with the Bills, Wilson will push for a high-end WR2 designation this week. 
 -  Kyle Dvorchak

 St. Brown played through the rib injury last week. He remained limited in all three practices before this week’s game. He’s likely not at full strength, but there was never much risk of him missing today’s game. He remains a high-end WR1.
